cards.f: Two ways to increase added value
cards.b: Raise the price (branding, packaging, service) or cut the cost of materials (cheaper supplier, less waste).
Primary: extracting natural resources. Secondary: manufacturing and construction. Tertiary: services.

short.q: Explain why added value is not the same as profit. [2]
short.model: Added value is selling price minus the cost of bought-in materials, so it ignores other costs. Wages, rent and other overheads must still be paid from it before profit is reached.
points: other costs (wages, rent) still to be paid

short.q: State two disadvantages of being a sole trader. [2]
short.model: Unlimited liability and limited capital (also: long hours, no continuity).
points: limited finance / long hours / no continuity

short.q: Explain two reasons why the tertiary sector has grown in developed economies. [4]
short.model: Rising incomes lead people to spend more on services such as tourism. Competition from lower-cost manufacturers abroad cuts secondary jobs, so workers move into services.
points: rising incomes, more spending on services

short.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to a franchisee of buying a franchise. [4]
short.model: Advantage: well-known brand gives sales quickly and lower risk. Disadvantage: pays fees and royalties and has little freedom to change the business.

short.q: A business wants to raise $2 million for a new factory. Explain one reason why becoming a plc might help and one reason why it might not. [4]
short.model: As a plc it can sell shares to the public to raise large sums with limited liability. However, it is costly to set up, must publish accounts and owners may lose control through takeover.
points: can sell shares to the public / large capital
loss of control by original owners
